author: granite state times
title: NFIB urges New Hampshire lawmakers to support employment tax relief in HB 155
text:
The National Federation of Independent Business in New Hampshire called on May 29 for state lawmakers to support the employment tax relief measures proposed in the conference report on House Bill 155. The organization, which represents more than 1,700 small businesses in the state, said the provisions would provide significant benefits to small employers.
“Reducing the state’s employment tax burden would be a major win for small employers in New Hampshire,” said John Reynolds, NFIB New Hampshire State Director. “The Business Enterprise Tax is a financial drag on small employers that makes it more expensive to hire workers and increase compensation. Exempting thousands of additional small employers from the BET and using future surpluses to lower the tax rate is a fiscally responsible plan for helping Main Street businesses hire, grow, and thrive in the Granite State.”
The committee of conference report on HB 155 includes three main provisions: raising the Business Enterprise Tax filing threshold from $300,000 to $400,000 in enterprise value—which is expected to exempt an estimated additional 4,500 small employers from filing a return; reducing the BET rate by 0.05% for every $100 million in combined surplus business tax revenue until it reaches its original level of 0.25%; and appropriating $2.5 million to increase per diem nursing home rates and draw down additional federal matching funds.
The National Federation of Independent Business strengthens New Hampshire communities by supporting the small business sector and represents more than 1,700 members across the state through education and legislative engagement with policymakers, according to its official website.
For over eight decades, NFIB has advocated for America’s independent business owners at both federal and state levels as a nonprofit and nonpartisan organization dedicated exclusively to advancing priorities for small businesses.
